about: Mezcal Trascendente is a family project from Oaxaca’s Central Valleys, the pride of the Bianciardi-Salcido family and made with a fifth-generation maestro mezcalero. Launched in 2020, it works from the old Oaxaca–Tehuantepec highway near Tlacolula de Matamoros, close to Yagul, the UNESCO-listed archaeological site whose mineral-rich spring water the brand uses. Its agaves are grown by native communities of the valley, and the mezcal reached the United States in 2025 through Spiribam America, its first mezcal.

This joven is made entirely from Espadín (Agave angustifolia), harvested at maturity. The hearts are roasted in a volcanic-stone pit oven over sweet wood from the Sierra Juárez, with care taken to limit how much combustion smoke reaches the agave. Fermentation is slow and wild, driven by natural yeasts, and the mezcal is distilled twice in copper pot stills. It is bottled unaged, as a mezcal artesanal, at 40% alcohol.

The aim is a fresher, less smoke-driven mezcal. Tasting notes from the brand’s US listings lead with citrus, orange leaf, mandarin and lemon tea, then cedar, a clear minerality and only a subtle thread of smoke on a long finish. The producer positions it as an aperitif, and it shows its character best neat or in a simple, spirit-forward cocktail.
facts: Volcanic-stone pit oven, Sierra Juárez sweet wood
